value.rationale: Dispersal is an ecologically motivated decision variable whose ability to moderate local variability can conflict with global aggregate behavior. Bipartite migration has a negative eigenmode that makes full migration nonoptimal; an exact all-size convex classification, universal 4-patch minimizer, strict memory dependence, and size expansion give substantial structural information beyond a single optimization example. The invariant spatial-mean variance shows the distinction between local and regional effects. The precise result is for linear isotropic environmental fluctuations and is not asserted to predict extinction.
